category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title and rationale focus only on Lesson 1's snapshot/trend trap; no field cross-references Lesson 2's balance scale arc or names how change/stay-the-same seeds the equality work coming up. lesson_arc bridge is implicit only.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit forward-bridge sentence in expanded_walkthrough.rationale or consolidation.discussion_prompts: 'Tomorrow Bella brings out the balance scale — when two amounts STAY THE SAME on each side, the scale balances. Today's stay-the-same idea sets that up.' Mirror this in the worksheet teacher_notes.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale describes the snapshot vs trend trap concretely but does not cite or align with named research (e.g., Carpenter & Levi 2000 on early algebraic reasoning, Kaput on variable, or Empson). recovery_moves are concrete but do not branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Carpenter & Levi (2000) 'Developing Conceptions of Algebraic Reasoning' in expanded_walkthrough.rationale. Branch recovery_moves: if child cites today's count, use the 'was Sarah here last Tuesday?' counter; if child cannot name any varying quantity, drop to a body example (fingers up now vs after wiggling).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials requires a 'Per-pair set of 24 photo cards' and 'Anchor chart with two columns'; differentiation does not include an explicit no-paper, no-prep alternative path using only voice, body, or gesture so the lesson can run on a day with zero prep.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add to differentiation a no-materials variant: 'No-paper version — teacher calls out a quantity (number of children today / sides on a square / weather). Children point THUMBS-UP for STAYS THE SAME and WIGGLE-FINGERS for CHANGES. Sort 12 spoken quantities this way; no cards required.' This makes the lesson runnable any day.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Bella anchors minds_on/action/consolidation and vocabulary is child-friendly with 'I can' criteria, but there is no distinctive quotable refrain or memorable chant. consolidation.exit_routine is a sticky-note write, not a chant the children carry between lessons.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Bella a recurring refrain children echo. Example: 'Bella's question — does it CHANGE or STAY?' with a hand-sign (open palm = change, fist = stay). Add to consolidation.exit_routine: 'Children chant Bella's refrain three times before leaving the carpet.' Quote the refrain in teacher_script and reuse in Lessons 2-5 character_continuity.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Part 1 uses 12 cards but the lesson Station A uses 16; lesson Action step 1 sorts a different set of 6 specific cards (number of pets, doors in school, birthday month, books in bag, provinces, temperature) — only some overlap with the worksheet's 12. Part 3 Why-prompt is a transfer task but no justification is recorded.
category_feedback.required_fix: Either align worksheet Part 1's 12 cards to be a subset of the lesson's 16 (so worksheet practises the SAME cards) plus 2 deliberate transfer items, OR add teacher_notes line: 'Part 3 is a transfer task — children apply the WHY reasoning from the expanded_walkthrough to a self-chosen quantity, verifying generalisation.' Match counts and document the variation.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression (definition vs lived experience) is explicit and vocabulary is precise, but the lesson does not let children invent or compare strategies — sorting is the only activity. expanded_walkthrough names the snapshot trap but not in research-grounded terms (Carpenter & Levi CGI early-algebra framing, Kaput on variable as varying quantity).
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an Action step where pairs INVENT their own change-vs-stay categories beyond the cards (e.g., 'find a quantity in the room nobody else thought of'), then COMPARE: which pair's example is the most surprising stay-the-same? Why? Cite Carpenter & Levi's variable-as-varying-quantity framing in expanded_walkthrough.rationale.

summary: Pair 1 is solidly Achieving across all six categories but does not clear the Exceeding bar in any. Bella anchors the lesson, the snapshot vs trend trap is real and concrete, materials are mostly everyday with optional puppets, and worksheet parts map to success criteria. Gaps: no forward-bridge to Lesson 2's balance scale, no research citations (Carpenter & Levi / Kaput), no no-paper alternative, no quotable refrain, no strategy invention, and worksheet card count diverges from lesson Station A. Six 3s means revise both lesson and worksheet.
